reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended A full wrapper queue delays source-error propagation, allowing reads after abort to return buffered data and leaving the shared signal listener attached after a network failure while reading is paused.
1 open issue - [Forward source errors immediately when the wrapper queue is full](https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/pull/1137#discussion_r4567224531) · New
What changed in this PR This PR addresses #1135 by updating web-client cancellation so concurrent requests can share an abort signal without replacing the caller’s handler. **Changes:** - Replaces `onabort` assignment with per-request event listeners. - Adds response-body wrapping to manage listener cleanup. - Adds regression tests and a web-client changelog entry. The change preserves public API signatures and introduces no apparent security-sensitive behavior. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `packages/​client-web/​src/​connection/​web_connection.ts` | Updates abort subscriptions and response-body cleanup. | | `packages/​client-web/​CHANGELOG.md` | Documents the shared-signal cancellation fix. | | `packages/​client-web/​__tests__/​unit/​web_shared_abort_signal.test.ts` | Tests shared cancellation, caller handlers, body reads, and listener cleanup. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: When the wrapper's one-chunk queue is full, a source error is not forwarded until the caller reads again, so a read after abort can return buffered data instead of rejecting. A network failure also leaves the shared signal's listener attached while the caller pauses reading. Observe `reader.closed` rejection to release the listener and error the wrapper immediately, and add a regression test that errors the source while the wrapper queue is full.
